thread:
lina: quick check-in: we hit a weird case in staging where policy kept picking a cheaper model variant even though regional latency spiked. thinking of adding a 'staleness_penalty' derived from probe_age to the operational_score.

tom: what did the probe_age look like?

lina: some API proxies hadn't reported for ~45s due to a deploy; probe_age was 60-70s in that region. our operational score didn't account for staleness, so the old low-latency estimate persisted.
om: staleness penalty makes sense. maybe exponential decay over time so old samples quickly lose weight.

infra-bot: note: adding decay parameters increases the tuning surface. add to RFC checklist.

lina: proposed formula: op_score_adj = op_score_raw * exp(-probe_age / T) where T is staleness_half_life parameter. default T=10s.
tom: default T=10s seems short; for some backends probes are noisy at 5s frequency. maybe default 30s for safety.
lina: fair. we should expose tenant-level overrides.
om: also add confidence band: if probe_count < N, set confidence low and prefer safer route.

infra-bot: action: instrument probe_age distribution and run sim to see impact on p95.
tom: i'll add dashboard for probe_age and regions with >30s median.
lina: implementation path: add staleness term to circuit layer (if present) else policy fallback applies it. also add a test in the sim harness that injects probe blackhole and ensures system flips within expected time.

om: sounds good. one more thing: when we apply decay, also record in explain payload the probe_age and applied penalty so ops can understand flips.

lina: agreed. will add to RFC. finish notes and share.
